QASHANI:101:6-10/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:101:6-10/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:101:6-10/r1.claim: Heavy scales are real sciences, psychic virtues, and heart and spirit perfections; their owner has a satisfied, true life in gardens of attributes above gardens of deeds.
QASHANI:101:6-10/r1.anchor: من العلوم الحقيقية والفضائل النفسانية والكمالات القلبية والروحانية

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p421/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p421/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p421/r4.claim: Only deeds will help: God weighs them in a just balance, granting eternal bliss when good deeds outweigh evil and Hell when the scales tip the other way.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p421/r4.anchor: God will set up the Balance of Justice in which all of man’s deeds will be weighed.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p424/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p424/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p424/r4.claim: Only deeds matter on that Day; good deeds that outweigh evil bring salvation, while the rest doom their bearers, and a special balance weighs human deeds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p424/r4.anchor: meant only to weigh the deeds of men

QUSHAYRI:v3p444/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p444/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p444/r8.claim: Those whose scales are heavy with good deeds will have a pleasing life; “pleasing” means made pleasing to them.
QUSHAYRI:v3p444/r8.anchor: من ثقلت موازينه بالخيرات فهو في عيشة راضية ؛ أي مرضية

QUSHAYRI:v3p444/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p444/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p444/r9.claim: One account says deeds are weighed through the weighing of their written records.
QUSHAYRI:v3p444/r9.anchor: ووزن الأعمال يومئذ يكون بوزن الصحف

QUSHAYRI:v3p444/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p444/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p444/r10.claim: Another account says a substance will be created for each component of a person's acts, and those substances will be weighed as the deeds' measure.
QUSHAYRI:v3p444/r10.anchor: ويقال : يخلق بدل كل جزء من أفعاله جوهرا

SULAMI:v2p416/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p416/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p416/r1.claim: In answer to whether deeds make scales heavy, the Wāsiṭī says God makes them heavy or light as He wills; a report says the scales are in God's hand, who raises and lowers people according to pre-eternal decree.
SULAMI:v2p416/r1.anchor: وقيل للواسطي رحمه الله : هل يجوز أن تثقل الموازين بأعمالنا فإن لو جاز ذلك لا من كل من كثرت أعماله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p511#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p511#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p511#2/r7.claim: The person with heavy scales lives in a pleasing life in Paradise.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p511#2/r7.anchor: فهو في عيشة راضية} مرضية في الجنة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p511#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p511#2/r8.speaker: الزجاج
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p511#2/r8.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains radiya as possessing contentment: the person is pleased with that life.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p511#2/r8.anchor: قال الزجاج ذات رضا يرضاها صاحبها

BAYDAWI-FULL:101:1-11/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:101:1-11/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:101:1-11/r5.claim: The person enjoys a life that is itself pleasing or is pleasing to its inhabitant.
BAYDAWI-FULL:101:1-11/r5.anchor: { فهو فى عيشة } في عيش. { راضية } ذات رضا أو مرضية

BIQAI-FULL:v8p514/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p514/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p514/r4.claim: A person whose good deeds outweigh falsehood enters a life of lasting, consistent pleasure; rāḍiya can mean either possessing satisfaction or being pleasing.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p514/r4.anchor: { فهو } بسبب رجحان حسناته { في عيشة } أي حياة تتقلب فيها

NAHHAS:v5p280/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p280/r9.speaker: مجاهد
NAHHAS:v5p280/r9.claim: He says the person will be pleased with the life.

NAHHAS:v5p280/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p280/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p280/r10.claim: The Arabic construction means ‘a life possessing satisfaction,’ a relational adjective.
NAHHAS:v5p280/r10.anchor: قال أبو جعفر التقدير في العربية ذات رضى على النسب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p516#3/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p516#3/r12.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p516#3/r12.claim: Al-Khalil and Sibawayh explain radiyah as a possessive adjective: a life possessing satisfaction.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p516#3/r12.anchor: معناه: ذات رضى على النسب، وهذا قول الخليل وسيبويه،

JISHUMI:v10p7519/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7519/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7519/r8.claim: Rāḍiya has a passive sense, “pleasing,” or means “possessing satisfaction,” like other active forms used for what someone has.
JISHUMI:v10p7519/r8.anchor: راضية أي: مرضية، فاعل بمعنى مفعول، على تقدير: ذات رضا

JISHUMI:v10p7519/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7519/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7519/r9.claim: Two poetic examples support using an active form to mean “possessing” something, as in “possessing hardship” or “possessing dates.”
JISHUMI:v10p7519/r9.anchor: قال الشاعر: كليني لهم يا أميمة ناصب

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p328/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p328/r3.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p328/r3.claim: Qatada says the approved life is a pleasing life, namely Paradise.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p328/r3.anchor: أحدهما : يعني في عيشة مرضية , قال قتادة : وهي الجنة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p328/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p328/r4.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p328/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says it is lasting bliss.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p328/r4.anchor: الثاني : في نعيم دائم , قاله الضحاك , فيكون على الوجه الأول من المعاش

MUQATIL:101:7-8/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:101:7-8/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:101:7-8/r1.claim: Only sincere monotheists make their scales heavy by saying there is no god but God; they enjoy a pleasing life in Paradise and never become dissatisfied there.
MUQATIL:101:7-8/r1.anchor: ولا يثقل الميزان إلا قول: لا إله إلا الله بقلوب المخلصين في الأعمال

QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r5.claim: A pleased life can mean a life that is pleasing to its owner.
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r5.anchor: ومعنى { عيشة راضية } أي عيش مرضي، يرضاه صاحبه.

QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r6.claim: Alternatively the life itself actively gives satisfaction by its softness and submission to its occupants; Paradise's raised couches lower for a saint and rise afterward.
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r6.anchor: وقيل: { عيشة راضية } أي فاعلة للرضا، وهو اللين والانقياد لأهلها.

QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r7.claim: Paradise's fruit branches lower toward a saint when desired, illustrating the Qur'anic description of near fruit.
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r7.anchor: فإذا اشتهى ولي الله ثمرتها تدلت إليه، حتى يتناولها ولي الله قاعدا وقائما

QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r8.claim: A report says a saint's staff makes a river flow without a channel through his palaces and gathering places wherever he wishes.
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r8.anchor: فيروى في الخبر «إنه يشير بقضيبه فيجري من غير أخدود حيث شاء من قصوره وفي مجالسه».

ZAJJAJ:v5p355/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p355/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p355/r6.claim: Some gloss rāḍiyah as “pleasing,” which returns to the same exegetical meaning: a life that satisfies its inhabitant.
ZAJJAJ:v5p355/r6.anchor: وقال قوم: معناه مرضية، وهو يعود إلى هذا المعنى في التفسير.

STUDYQURAN:101:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:101:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:101:intro/r3.claim: The final six verses contrast the recompense of those whose scales are heavy with good deeds and those whose scales are light.
STUDYQURAN:101:intro/r3.anchor: The last six verses (vv. 6–11) contrast the recompense

STUDYQURAN:101:6/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r8.claim: The contenting life of the person with heavy scales is linked to 69:21.
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r8.anchor: For he shall enjoy a life contenting, cf. 69:21.

ASAD-NOTES:101:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:101:intro/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:101:intro/r1.claim: This is an early Meccan surah, probably revealed after At-Tin (surah 95).
ASAD-NOTES:101:intro/r1.anchor: An early Meccan surah, most probably revealed after surah 95 (At-Tin)

TABATABAI:101:1-9/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:101:1-9/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:101:1-9/r1.claim: The Meccan surah warns and gives glad tidings about resurrection, with warning as its dominant tone.
TABATABAI:101:1-9/r1.anchor: بيان إنذار وتبشير بالقيامة يغلب فيه جانب الانذار، والسورة مكية

TABATABAI:101:1-9/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:101:1-9/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:101:1-9/r12.claim: In 'a satisfying life,' 'life' with kasra is a noun of kind like sitting; calling the life satisfied is figurative attribution, or means a life possessing satisfaction.
TABATABAI:101:1-9/r12.anchor: العيشة بكسر العين كالجلسة بناء نوع، وتوصيفها براضية - والراضي صاحبها - من المجاز العقلي

TABRISI:101:5-11/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:101:5-11/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:101:5-11/r5.claim: A pleasing life is one its owner is content with.
TABRISI:101:5-11/r5.anchor: أي معيشة ذات رضى يرضاها صاحبها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r5.claim: Abu Ishaq explains a pleasing life as one of satisfaction that its possessor likes, using possessive adjective patterns.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r5.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: أي ذات رضى يرضاها صاحبها (¬6)، وهي كقولهم: لابن، ونابل، وتامر.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r6.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r6.claim: Abu Bakr explains such forms as meaning 'possessing milk, merit, and dates'; commentators therefore gloss the life as pleasing to its owner.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r6.anchor: (قال أبو بكر) (¬7): بمعنى ذو لبن، ونبل، وتمر (¬8)، ولهذا قال المفسرون في تفسيرها: "مرضية" (¬9) على معنى يرضاها صاحبها.

ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r2.claim: Calling the life rādiyah rather than marḍiyyah is rhetorically emphatic: the life so fully satisfies its worthy owner that it surrounds him with lasting contentment.
ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r2.anchor: rızânın tasavvurlar fevkinde olan kemâlini belâgatle ifade ederek sâhibinin o hayâta ehliyet-i kâmilesini

ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r3.speaker: Âlûsî
ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r3.claim: Alusi says the familiar reading takes rādiyah as a relational form, meaning a life characterized by satisfaction.
ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r3.anchor: Âlûsî der ki: “Meşhur olan burada ‘râzıye’ nisbet bâbından olmaktır

ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r4.claim: Rādiyah may also be understood as marḍiyyah by lexical or predicative metaphor, meaning a life its owner is pleased with.
ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r4.anchor: ‘râzıye’nin marzıyye mânasına olması da tecviz edilmiştir

ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r5.claim: Rhetoricians also allow a concealed and imaginative metaphor in the expression.
ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r5.anchor: bunda isti‘âre-i mekniye ve tahyîliye dahi tecviz edilmiştir.

ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r6.speaker: بعض الإجلة
ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r6.claim: Some eminent scholars object that relational forms are construed with dhū and are not made feminine because they attach to nouns rather than functioning as adjectives.
ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r6.anchor: bazı ecille burada nefis bir beyanda bulunmuş ve demiştir ki ‘niseb bâbından olanlar

ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r7.speaker: Sîrâfî
ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r7.claim: Sirafi gives three explanations for the feminine ending: the life stays attached to its people, the ending intensifies meaning as in rāwiya, or it preserves the word's form after loss of yā.
ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r7.anchor: Sonra demiştir ki: ‘Kabûle layık olan budur. Bunun hâsılı birkaç vecihle cevaptır.

ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r8.speaker: Sîrâfî
ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r8.claim: Sirafi says the intensive feminine ending is not limited to allāma and cites rāwiya as another example; misakka may be anomalous or analogical.
ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r8.anchor: Bu da ‘allâme’ gibi fe‘‘âl veznine muhtas değildir. Onun için ‘râviye’ ile de temsil eylemiştir.

ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r9.speaker: Âlûsî
ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r9.claim: Alusi praises Sirafi's analysis as a subtle explanation missing from most books.
ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r9.anchor: bunu hıfzet çünkü nefistir, kitapların ekserîsi ondan hâlîdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r1.claim: Mawazin may mean the things weighed, namely deeds; the translation prefers this reading.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r2.claim: Alternatively, mawazin is the plural of mizan, “scales,” but metonymically still means the deeds weighed.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r2.anchor: İkinci anlama göre de kelime kinaye olarak yine tartılan amelleri ifade eder

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r3.claim: Heavy deeds signify an abundance of good that earns God's approval and eternal happiness in richly provisioned Gardens.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r3.anchor: “Tartılan amellerin ağır gelmesi” hayır ve iyiliklerin fazla olmasını anlatmakta ve Allah’ın rızâsının bu sayede kazanılacağını göstermektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r5.claim: Since afterlife events are unseen beyond what revelation states, one cannot speculate about how deeds will actually be weighed or measured.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r5.anchor: amellerin nasıl tartılacağı veya ölçüleceği hakkında söz söylemek yahut fikir yürütmek ise mümkün değildir

IBNASHUR:101:7/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:101:7/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:101:7/r1.claim: Ibn Ashur says عيشة is a verbal noun from العيش, like خيفة from الخوف, and here means life.
IBNASHUR:101:7/r1.anchor: اسم مصدر العَيش كالخِيفة اسم للخوف

IBNASHUR:101:7/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:101:7/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:101:7/r2.claim: Calling the life راضية is a rational metaphor: its possessor is content with it, so the life is described that way because it causes contentment or is its time.
IBNASHUR:101:7/r2.anchor: ووصف الحياة ب { راضية } مجاز عقلي لأن الراضي صاحبها راض بها فوصفت به العيشة لأنها سبب الرضى أو زمان الرضى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p354#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p354#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p354#7/r1.claim: A life pleasing in itself may mean one filled with satisfaction or one that is made pleasing to its inhabitant.

QUTB-ZILAL:101:7/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:101:7/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:101:7/r1.claim: Quṭb leaves the pleasant life undescribed in detail so its shade of contentment is felt; this is the most restful bliss.
QUTB-ZILAL:101:7/r1.anchor: ويدعها مجملة بلا تفصيل ، توقع في الحس ظلال الرضى وهو أروح النعيم

RAZI-FULL:v32p70#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p70#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p70#2/r1.claim: ʿĪsha is a verbal noun meaning living, just as khīfa is a verbal noun meaning fear.
RAZI-FULL:v32p70#2/r1.anchor: فالعيشة مصدر بمعنى العيش ، كالخيفة بمعنى الخوف

RAZI-FULL:v32p70#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p70#2/r2.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v32p70#2/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj interprets rāḍiya as a life possessing satisfaction that its owner approves; the exegetes paraphrase it as pleasing to its owner.
RAZI-FULL:v32p70#2/r2.anchor: وأما الراضية فقال الزجاج : معناه أي عيشة ذات رضا يرضاها صاحبها وهي كقولهم لابن ، وتامر

TAB:101:7/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:101:7/r1.speaker: author
TAB:101:7/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī explains the contented life as a life in Paradise that the person is pleased with.
TAB:101:7/r1.anchor: يقول : في عيشة قد رضيها في الجنة

TAB:101:7/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:101:7/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB:101:7/r2.claim: Qatāda glosses the contented life as being in Paradise; the source gives no grading.
TAB:101:7/r2.anchor: عن قتادة { فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ رَاضِيَةٍ } يعني : في الجنة

WAHIDI-QT:101:7/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:101:7/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:101:7/r1.claim: A pleasing life is a life that its inhabitant is pleased with.

CORPUSCORANICUM:101:7:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:7:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:7:anmerkung/r1.claim: The wording parallels 69:21 and 88:9; other early Meccan uses of r-d-y occur at 93:5, 92:21, 89:28, and 53:26, giving the root an apparently consistent eschatological association.
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:7:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Die Wurzel ist offenbar durchgängig eschatologisch konnotiert.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r1.claim: The well-known interpretation takes rāḍiya as a relational adjective: the life is one endowed with contentment or satisfaction.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r1.anchor: المشهور جعل ذلك من باب النسب أي ذات رضا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r2.claim: He also allows rāḍiya as a figurative passive meaning pleasing or pleased-with, or a figurative attribution whose true subject is the life’s possessor.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r2.anchor: أن تكون راضية بمعنى المفعول أى مرضية على التجوز في الكلمة نفسها وأن يكون الاسناد مجازيا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r3.claim: A concealed metaphor with an imaginative metaphorical feature is another possible analysis, as discussed in works of rhetoric.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r3.anchor: وجوز ان يكون في الكلام استعارة مكنية وتخييلية على ماقرر في كتب المعاني

ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r4.speaker: بعض الاجلة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r4.claim: A distinguished scholar argues that relational adjectives mean ‘possessing such-and-such’ and therefore are not feminine, since they do not modify an expressed noun and are treated as nouns.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r4.anchor: ماكان للنسب يؤول بذي كذا فلا يؤنث لانه لم يجر على موصوف فالحق بالجوامد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r5.speaker: السيرافي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r5.claim: Al-Sīrāfī objects that the feminine h in ʿīsha rāḍiya challenges the claim that relational forms do not take feminine marking.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r5.anchor: نقل عن السيرافي انه قال يقدح فيما عللوا به سقوط الهاء في عيشة راضية

ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r6.speaker: السيرافي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r6.claim: One explanation makes the life pleased with its inhabitants, accompanying them and content with them.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r6.anchor: أن تكون بمعنى انها راضية أهلها فهي ملازمة لهم راضية بهم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r7.speaker: السيرافي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r7.claim: A second explanation treats the feminine h as an intensive suffix, as in ʿallāma and riwāya.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r7.anchor: والآخر أن تكون الهاء للمبالغة كعلامة ورواية

ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r8.speaker: السيرافي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r8.claim: The h may preserve the word’s form by preventing loss of yāʾ; similar weak adjectives and some forms otherwise not feminized show this usage.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r8.anchor: الهاء لزمت لئلا تسقط الياء فيخل بالبنية كناقة مشلية وكلبة مجرية

ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r9.claim: Alusi explains rāḍiya here as an active participle whose necessary implication is intended: whoever wants and accepts something necessarily stays with it; the attribution may also be figurative.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r9.anchor: راضية هنا فيه ليس من باب النسب بل هو اسم فاعل أريد به لازم معناه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r10.claim: He accepts intensive h as an explanation, noting that this suffix is not confined to the pattern faʿʿāl, as riwāya also shows.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r10.anchor: ان الهاء للمبالغة ولا تختص بفعال ولذا مثل برواية أيضا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r11.claim: He also accepts adding h to a weak adjective to preserve its form; misakka is either an irregular form or reflects geminates’ resemblance to weak roots.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222/r11.anchor: يجوز الحاق الهاء في المعتل لحفظ البنية ومصكة اما شاذا ولتشبه المضاعف بالمعتل

QASHANI:101:1-5/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:101:1-5/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:101:1-5/r5.claim: This annihilation reading does not fit the later distinction of heavy and light scales; in God’s scale, rising and ascending count as weight, while descent is lightness: enduring righteous deeds matter most, and perishable pleasures have no weight.

TAB-FULL:v24p594#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p594#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p594#2/r4.claim: Mujahid says the person is in a life he is pleased with in Paradise.
TAB-FULL:v24p594#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، {فهو في عيشة راضية} [الحاقة: 21] يقول «في عيشة قد رضيها في الجنة»

TAB-FULL:v24p594#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p594#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p594#2/r5.claim: Qatada glosses the pleasing life as Paradise.
TAB-FULL:v24p594#2/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، {فهو في عيشة راضية} [الحاقة: 21] يعني: في «الجنة»

TABATABAI:101:10-11/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:101:10-11/r7.speaker: القمي
TABATABAI:101:10-11/r7.claim: Al-Qummi glosses those whose scales are light as people with little good.
TABATABAI:101:10-11/r7.anchor: وفي قوله { وأما من خفت موازينه } قال من الحسنات

CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r5.claim: Riddling that creates rhetorical tension also structures oath sequences such as Q 100 and teaching questions at 90:12–16, 97:2–4, 101:1–11, and 104:5–9.
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r5.anchor: auf dem Einsatz von Änigmatisierung zur Erzeugung rhetorischer Spannung basieren aber auch Schwurserien wie zu Beginn von Q 100

ABUHAYYAN:101:6/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:101:6/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:101:6/r2.claim: The segment also refers the expression “a pleasing life” to Abu Hayyan's discussion of it in al-Haqqa.
ABUHAYYAN:101:6/r2.anchor: وتقدم الكلام في الموازين وثقلها وخفتها في الأعراف ، وعيشة راضية في الحاقة

ABUHAYYAN:101:7/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:101:7/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:101:7/r1.claim: Abu Hayyan again refers discussion of the scales and their heaviness and lightness to al-Aʿraf.
ABUHAYYAN:101:7/r1.anchor: وتقدم الكلام في الموازين وثقلها وخفتها في الأعراف

ABUHAYYAN:101:7/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:101:7/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:101:7/r2.claim: Abu Hayyan refers the expression “a pleasing life” to his discussion of it in al-Haqqa.
ABUHAYYAN:101:7/r2.anchor: وتقدم الكلام في الموازين وثقلها وخفتها في الأعراف ، وعيشة راضية في الحاقة

ALUSI:101:6/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:6/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:101:6/r1.claim: The passage summarizes the division of people into two groups and signals each group's particular state after describing what is common to all.
ALUSI:101:6/r1.anchor: بيان إجمالي لتحزب الناس حزبين وتنبيه على كيفية الأحوال الخاصة بكل منهما أثر بيان الأحوال الشاملة للكل

ALUSI:101:7/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:7/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:101:7/r1.claim: The common analysis takes rāḍiya as a relational adjective: a life characterized by satisfaction or delight.
ALUSI:101:7/r1.anchor: المشهور جعل ذلك من باب النسب أي ذات رضا

ALUSI:101:7/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:7/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:101:7/r2.claim: Rāḍiya can mean pleasing, with the word figurative for the passive sense or attribution transferred from the person enjoying the life.
ALUSI:101:7/r2.anchor: وجوز أن تكون { رَّاضِيَةٍ } بمعنى المفعول

ALUSI:101:7/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:7/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:101:7/r3.claim: A further proposal analyzes the expression as a concealed metaphor with an associated imaginative image.
ALUSI:101:7/r3.anchor: وجوز أن يكون في الكلام استعارة مكنية وتخييلية

ALUSI:101:7/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:7/r4.speaker: السيرافي
ALUSI:101:7/r4.claim: Al-Sirafi objects that relational adjectives are not normally feminine because they do not agree with an overt described noun, yet rāḍiya carries feminine hāʾ.
ALUSI:101:7/r4.anchor: ونقل عن السيرافي أنع قال يقدح

ALUSI:101:7/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:7/r5.speaker: السيرافي
ALUSI:101:7/r5.claim: Al-Sirafi offers two explanations: the life is pleased with its inhabitants and stays with them, or hāʾ marks intensity like ʿallāma and rāwiya.

ALUSI:101:7/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:7/r6.speaker: السيرافي
ALUSI:101:7/r6.claim: Al-Sirafi also suggests that the suffix preserves the form by preventing loss of yāʾ, and notes feminine hāʾ in forms such as nāqa mashliya and kalba mujriya.
ALUSI:101:7/r6.anchor: ووجه بأن الهاء لزمت لئلا تسقط الياء فيخل بالبنية كناقة مشلية وكلبة مجرية

ALUSI:101:7/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:7/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:101:7/r7.claim: Al-Alusi's first answer is that rāḍiya is not relational here: it is an active participle meaning what follows necessarily from choosing and being pleased, or a figurative attribution.
ALUSI:101:7/r7.anchor: أن راضية هنا فيه ليس من باب النسب بل هو اسم فاعل أريد به لازم معناه

ALUSI:101:7/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:7/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI:101:7/r8.claim: His second answer is that hāʾ can indicate intensity and is not restricted to the faʿʿāla pattern, as rāwiya shows.
ALUSI:101:7/r8.anchor: إن الهشاء للمبالغة ولا تختص بفعال ولذا مثل برواية

ALUSI:101:7/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:7/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI:101:7/r9.claim: His third answer allows hāʾ to preserve the form in a defective word and exceptionally in miṣakka, with a doubled form analogized to a weak one.
ALUSI:101:7/r9.anchor: أنه يجوز الحاق الهاء في المعتل لحفظ البلية

ALUSI:101:9/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:9/r8.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI:101:9/r8.claim: Al-Kashf calls the imprecation reading best because it matches the emphatic wording of the preceding pleasurable life; al-Tibi calls it clearest, though al-Alusi leaves room for discussion.

BAGHAWI:101:7/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:101:7/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:101:7/r1.claim: The person is in a pleasing, approved life in Paradise.
BAGHAWI:101:7/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى : { فهو في عيشة راضية } مرضية في الجنة

BAGHAWI:101:7/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:101:7/r2.speaker: الزجاج
BAGHAWI:101:7/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains the phrase as a life possessing satisfaction, one its owner is pleased with.
BAGHAWI:101:7/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج : ذات رضا يرضاها صاحبها

BAYDAWI:101:7/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:101:7/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:101:7/r1.claim: The life is endowed with satisfaction.

BAYDAWI:101:7/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:101:7/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:101:7/r2.claim: Alternatively, the life is pleasing to its inhabitant.

BIQAI:101:7/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:101:7/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:101:7/r1.claim: The blessed life is a life in which its inhabitant continually moves and lives.
BIQAI:101:7/r1.anchor: حسناته { في عيشة } أي حياة تتقلب فيها

BIQAI:101:7/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:101:7/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:101:7/r2.claim: The feminine form suggests a single, constant state of clarity and pleasure rather than the varied conditions of worldly life.
BIQAI:101:7/r2.anchor: ولعله ألحقها الهاء الدالة على الوحدة

BIQAI:101:7/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:101:7/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:101:7/r3.claim: The life either possesses satisfaction or is pleasing; its abode is the lofty Garden.
BIQAI:101:7/r3.anchor: { راضية * } أي ذات رضى ،   أو مرضية

BIQAI:101:9/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:101:9/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:101:9/r4.claim: Al-Hāwiya is an extremely low, descending fire in which he keeps falling; the passage omits a hostile life in the second clause and a mother in the first.

DURR:101:6/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:101:6/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR:101:6/r3.claim: Qatada identifies the heavy-scale person's pleasing life as Paradise.
DURR:101:6/r3.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله : { يوم يكون الناس كالفراش المبثوث }

DURR:101:8/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:101:8/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR:101:8/r3.claim: Qatada identifies the heavy-scale person's pleasing life as Paradise.
DURR:101:8/r3.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله : { يوم يكون الناس كالفراش المبثوث }

DURR:101:9/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:101:9/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR:101:9/r3.claim: Qatada identifies the heavy-scale person's pleasing life as Paradise.
DURR:101:9/r3.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله : { يوم يكون الناس كالفراش المبثوث }

IBNATIYYA:101:7/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:101:7/r1.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
IBNATIYYA:101:7/r1.claim: Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh explain rāḍiya as a life endowed with satisfaction, an attributive construction expressing relation.
IBNATIYYA:101:7/r1.anchor: { عيشة راضية } معناه : ذات رضى على النسب ، وهذا قول الخليل وسيبويه

IBNKATHIR:101:7/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:101:7/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:101:7/r1.claim: A pleasing life means life in Paradise.
IBNKATHIR:101:7/r1.anchor: فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ رَاضِيَةٍ } يعني : في الجنة

MAWARDI:101:7/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:101:7/r1.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI:101:7/r1.claim: Qatada takes the phrase as a pleasing life, namely Paradise.
MAWARDI:101:7/r1.anchor: أحدهما : يعني في عيشة مرضية ،   قال قتادة : وهي الجنة .

MAWARDI:101:7/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:101:7/r2.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI:101:7/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak understands it as lasting bliss, construing it from ʿaysh (life) rather than maʿash (livelihood).
MAWARDI:101:7/r2.anchor: الثاني : في نعيم دائم ،   قاله الضحاك ،   فيكون على الوجه الأول من المعاش ،   وعلى الوجه الثاني من العيش .

NASAFI:101:7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:101:7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:101:7/r1.claim: The life is either endowed with pleasure or itself pleasing and approved.

QURTUBI:101:7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:101:7/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:101:7/r1.claim: One meaning is a pleasing life that its owner is satisfied with.
QURTUBI:101:7/r1.anchor: { عيشة راضية } أي عيش مرضي ،   يرضاه صاحبه .

QURTUBI:101:7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:101:7/r2.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:101:7/r2.claim: Another reading makes the life itself the giver of satisfaction: it is gentle and compliant with its inhabitants.
QURTUBI:101:7/r2.anchor: وقيل : { عيشة راضية } أي فاعلة للرضا ،   وهو اللين والانقياد لأهلها .

QURTUBI:101:7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:101:7/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI:101:7/r3.claim: Paradise’s raised couches, about a hundred years high, lower for a friend of God to sit on and then rise again.
QURTUBI:101:7/r3.anchor: فالعيشة كلمة تجمع النعم التي في الجنة ،   فهي فاعلة للرضا ،   كالفرش المرفوعة ،   وارتفاعها مقدار مائة عام ،

QURTUBI:101:7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:101:7/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI:101:7/r4.claim: A tree’s high branches bend its fruit within reach when the friend of God desires it, whether sitting or standing.
QURTUBI:101:7/r4.anchor: فإذا اشتهى ولي الله ثمرتها تدلت إليه ،   حتى يتناولها ولي الله قاعدا وقائما ،   وذلك قوله تعالى : { قطوفها دانية }{[16327]} [ الحاقة : 23 ] .

QURTUBI:101:7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:101:7/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI:101:7/r5.claim: Wherever the friend of God walks or moves, a river runs with him in whatever direction he wants, above or below.
QURTUBI:101:7/r5.anchor: وحيثما مشى أو ينتقل من مكان إلى مكان ،   جرى معه نهر حيث شاء ،   علوا وسفلا ،   وذلك قوله تعالى : { يفجرونها تفجيرا }{[16328]} [ الإنسان : 6 ] .

QURTUBI:101:7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:101:7/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI:101:7/r6.claim: A report says he points with his staff and a river flows without a channel wherever he wants among his palaces and halls.
QURTUBI:101:7/r6.anchor: فيروى في الخبر ( إنه يشير بقضيبه فيجري من غير أخدود حيث شاء من قصوره وفي مجالسه ) .

QURTUBI:101:7/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:101:7/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI:101:7/r7.claim: These blessings make the life itself seem to grant satisfaction, yielding freely and generously to its inhabitants.
QURTUBI:101:7/r7.anchor: فهذه الأشياء كلها عيشة قد أعطت الرضا من نفسها ،   فهي فاعلة للرضا ،   وهي أنزلت وانقادت بذلا وسماحة .

RAZI:101:7/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:101:7/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:101:7/r1.claim: ʿĪsha is a verbal noun meaning living or life, just as khīfa means fear.
RAZI:101:7/r1.anchor: فالعيشة مصدر بمعنى العيش ، كالخيفة بمعنى الخوف

RAZI:101:7/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:101:7/r2.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI:101:7/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains rāḍiya as a life possessing satisfaction, one its owner approves, like labin and tāmir meaning possessing milk and dates; commentators gloss it as pleasing to its owner.
RAZI:101:7/r2.anchor: فقال الزجاج : معناه أي عيشة ذات رضا يرضاها صاحبها وهي كقولهم لابن وتامر
